waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-23 re-check under AWH's high-water-edge ruling (curation doc open-apron rule). High water: Reclamation Pathfinder Reservoir allocations sheet (rev. 2016-05-19; UNT web archive capture 2016-12-24 of usbr.gov/gp/aop/resaloc/pathfinder.pdf): top of active conservation = uncontrolled spillway crest 5,852.49 ft (1,783.84 m), the edge used in the Sage 13585 re-check, where the USGS 3DEP 1,783.84 m contour follows the vegetation/sand line (2022) and the 2011 water. Pads: the 2023 rebuild is on today's Esri World_Imagery here (GE01 2023-09-30, 0.46 m; Esri Wayback release 43291): concrete pads with dark-roofed shelters on a new road layout, where the WV02 2022-09-19 capture (release 37965) still shows the old green-roofed shelters on dirt; 11 sheltered pads counted, matching Rec1's DB Site 01-11. The county's 'Diabase Campground Map' (natronacounty-wy.gov DocumentCenter/View/8097, linked from Rec1) is 403 and has no Wayback capture (checked 2026-11-23), and Rec1's per-site photos are sign-post close-ups, so pads are named by position, not DB number. Frames, all rendered: Esri at 450 m half-width (0.9 m/px), 150 m (0.3 m/px) and three 70 m frames (0.23 m/px) over the northeast row, the middle and the southwest lane, each with the 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM in the same EPSG:3857 frame and its 1,783.84 m contour drawn; Wayback 2011-06-22 (UC-G 0.3 m, release 25521) shows high water at the foot of the terrace. Measured shelter/pad to the 1,783.84 m edge, pad height above it, and the bank's steepest 3 m (median of five transects), reservoir side of the roads from northeast to southwest: NE-end pad (42.46924,-106.86982) ~16 m, +1.6 m, 13%, but straight through a cottonwood clump; (42.46908,-106.87004) ~15 m, +3.7 m, 54%; (42.46888,-106.87041) ~12 m, +3.3 m, 71%; (42.46858,-106.87072) ~13 m, +3.1 m, 53%; (42.46846,-106.87090) ~12 m, +2.8 m, 54%; on the southwest lane at the north end of a tree clump (42.46810,-106.87135) ~11 m, +1.0 m, 10%; at its south end (42.46756,-106.87183) ~7 m, +2.0 m, 52%. Between each of the last six and the edge: open, unused ground with low sage and scattered shrubs; no road, day use or tree screen. The three inner pads (42.46821,-106.87162; 42.46805,-106.87175; 42.46791,-106.87185) sit 32-36 m back behind the lane and the tree clump, and the pad north of the marina road (42.46895,-106.87115) 61 m back and 8.8 m up. Bank: the northeast row is on a terrace 2.8-3.7 m above full pool whose edge drops 1.3-2.2 m at about 28-35 degrees, steeper than Sage's accepted shore (pads 1.8-2.1 m up, steepest 3 m 25-42%) but a low bank, not a bluff; the lidar predates the 2023 pad work. In the 2023 frame the water stood ~100 m (marina bay) to ~200 m from the pads. Result: lakefront at six of the seven reservoir-side pads, with the drawdown caveat. The stored 'sites on the bench' read is superseded. --Claude
note: Natrona County campground west of Pathfinder Dam off County Road 409, beside the boat ramp, dock and Pathfinder Marina. Lakefront at six of the seven pads on the reservoir side of the campground roads, on open ground above a low bank at the high-water line; the pad at the northeast end looks at the water through trees, and the three inner pads and the one north of the road are set back. Water levels vary greatly: in a low year the water is 100-200 m from the pads, and the county says it can be 1,500 feet off. No cell service at the sites, so reserve before setting out. --Claude

waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-23 re-check under AWH's high-water-edge ruling (curation doc open-apron rule). High water: Reclamation Pathfinder Reservoir allocations sheet (rev. 2016-05-19; UNT web archive capture 2016-12-24 of usbr.gov/gp/aop/resaloc/pathfinder.pdf): top of active conservation = uncontrolled spillway crest 5,852.49 ft (1,783.84 m), the edge used in the Sage 13585 re-check, where the USGS 3DEP 1,783.84 m contour follows the vegetation/sand line (2022) and the 2011 water. Frames, all rendered: Esri World_Imagery (WV02 2022-09-19, a drawdown year) at 150 m half-width (0.3 m/px) and 70 m half-width (0.23 m/px) over the south and west shore, each with the 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM in the same EPSG:3857 frame and its 1,783.84 m contour drawn; Esri Wayback 2011-06-22 (UC-G 0.3 m, release 25521; z18 and z19) and 2020-06-05 (WV02, release 11475; z19). The 2011 frame has the water at the shelter fronts along the south and west shore, where the contour runs on the 2022 frame. Rec1 lists one 'Weiss Non-Reservable Sites' facility with no site names, so shelters are named by position. Measured shelter to the 1,783.84 m edge, pad height above it, and the bank's steepest 3 m (median of five transects): south shore outside the loop road, west shelter (42.46805,-106.86074) ~15 m, +2.1 m, 31%, and middle shelter (42.46797,-106.86038) ~11 m, +1.3 m, 21%, both over open, unused bare ground with a post and a shrub, no road or tree screen; east shelter (42.46803,-106.86012, plain on 2011 and 2020) ~13 m, +1.0 m, but under and behind a shore tree on the 2022 frame; west shore outside the loop road (42.46870,-106.86133) ~20 m, +3.5 m, 46%, over sparse sage with scattered small trees to the south. Inside the loop road the shelters are 26-51 m back with the road between (42.46841,-106.86093 ~26 m; 42.46854,-106.86069 ~51 m; 42.46826,-106.86008 ~30 m behind the road and the tree belt) and the north ones farther. In 2022 the water was ~115-140 m from the south shelters; in 2011 ~5-10 m. Result: lakefront at the two south-shore shelters and the west-shore shelter, with the drawdown caveat; the earlier 'loop in cottonwoods above the reservoir beach' read was the interior. --Claude
note: Natrona County campground on Pathfinder Reservoir just west of Pathfinder Dam, off County Road 409 (Pathfinder Road); the closest campground to the dam and its interpretive trail. Sheltered and open sites, ADA sites, restrooms, no drinking water; the RV dump is a quarter mile away on the county road. Lakefront at three sheltered sites outside the loop road, the two at the west end of the south shore and the one on the west shore, on open ground at the high-water line; the shelter at the east end of the south shore stands behind a tree, and the sites inside the loop are set back. Water levels vary greatly: in a low year the water is 100 m or more from the shore sites, and the county says it can be 1,500 feet off. --Claude
